summary: M.S. Computer Engineering graduate from Rochester Institute of Technology (RIT), NY. Builds C++ embedded firmware for microcontroller systems, from register-level STM32 bare-metal drivers to FreeRTOS task coordination with mutexes and interrupt-driven serial communication. Experienced implementing peripheral drivers directly against electrical schematics and datasheets, including custom PCB fabrication, I2C multiplexing, and sensor integration, and debugging at the hardware-software boundary with oscilloscopes and logic analyzers. Comfortable across embedded Linux platforms, including NVIDIA Jetson, for real-time system integration.

experience.title: Embedded Systems Intern
bullets: Developed a wearable gesture recognition glove integrating ADXL345 accelerometers with a Raspberry Pi and HC-05 Bluetooth to translate hand motion into HID cursor commands.
Implemented a custom tap detection algorithm using z-axis differential thresholding; resolved sensor jitter through software calibration and resolution tuning.

experience.title: General Secretary
bullets: Led a 25-member robotics team across national-level competitions, owning mechanical design, PCB fabrication, and firmware integration end to end.
Designed and fabricated custom single-layer PCBs in EAGLE for locomotive robots; implemented sensor communication over UART and I2C with closed-loop feedback.

projects.name: STM32 Bare-Metal Temperature Monitor
bullets: Built a Cortex-M4 temperature monitoring firmware in embedded C with timer-synchronized sensing and real-time display.
Implemented timer-triggered ADC scan conversions, interrupt-driven sample capture, and a low-level I2C driver.
Programmed peripherals directly in bare-metal C (GPIO, TIM2, ADC1, I2C1); achieved 3.68 KB Flash / 1.58 KB RAM at a deterministic 1 Hz update rate, verified in Proteus.

projects.name: Object Tracking Turret
bullets: Used YOLOv8 on an NVIDIA Jetson to detect and track objects, sending control commands to an STM32 over UART.
Implemented multi-servo PWM control with interrupt-driven UART commands and user override.
Used FreeRTOS with mutexes for shared-memory task coordination; integrated VL53L0X ToF sensing and OLED distance visualization.

projects.name: Voice-Controlled Robotic Arm (COFFIN) — MS Capstone, RIT
bullets: Built a vision-guided pick-and-place system across a mobile client, edge server, and a Jetson and Arduino controller pair linked by a unified WebSocket fabric.
Integrated dual VL53L0X ToF sensors (camera range-gate and gripper-triggered close at 25 mm) for contact-aware grasping via a TCA9548A I2C multiplexer.
Resolved 11 integration failures (false detections, servo brown-out, stale-frame capture); achieved 100% pick reliability (10/10 trials) at about 11.5 seconds end to end latency.
